title: Compensation for unlawful arrest or detention
summary: If you are unlawfully arrested or detained, the Constitution says you are entitled to compensation and a public apology from the appropriate authority.
body_plain: The Constitution provides that any person who is unlawfully arrested or detained is entitled to compensation and a public apology from the appropriate authority or person. This means an unlawful detention is not just wrong in principle - it can give you a legal claim. You enforce this by applying to a High Court, usually with the help of a lawyer or a legal aid organisation.
rights: If you are unlawfully arrested or detained, you are entitled to compensation and a public apology (s.35(6)).
You enforce this right by applying to a High Court (s.46).
Keep evidence of what happened to support a claim.
do_list: Write down dates, times, names, and any witnesses.
Keep any documents, medical reports, or photos.
Speak to a lawyer or Legal Aid about a claim.
dont_list: Do not throw away evidence of the detention.
Do not accept that nothing can be done about an unlawful detention.
